brief: Build a login page. A form with id `login-form` holds a text input with id `username`, a password input with id `password` and a button with id `login-btn` labelled "Sign in". On submit, use JavaScript to stop the submission; if either field is empty, show "Both fields are required" in an element with id `login-error`. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Submitting with an empty field shows the error message in #login-error
The layout stays usable at 360px width

brief: Build a contact form. A form with id `contact-form` has a text input with id `name`, an email input with id `email`, a textarea with id `message` and a button with id `send-btn` labelled "Send message". On submit, use JavaScript to prevent the page reload and write "Thanks, your message was noted" into a paragraph with id `status`.
behaviours: Submitting writes the thank-you text into #status without reloading the page
All four fields are visible and labelled

brief: Build a newsletter signup box. It has an email input with id `newsletter-email`, a button with id `subscribe-btn` labelled "Subscribe" and a paragraph with id `feedback`. When the button is clicked, write "Invalid email" into `feedback` unless the input contains an at sign, in which case write "You are subscribed". It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: An address without an at sign shows "Invalid email"
A valid-looking address shows "You are subscribed"

brief: Build a static customer survey page with no JavaScript. A form with id `survey` has the heading "Rate our service", three radio inputs (type radio) named `rating` for Good, Average and Poor, a textarea with id `comments`, and a button of type submit labelled "Submit". It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Three radio options are visible and only one can be chosen
The comments box sits below the options

brief: Build a static shipping address form with no JavaScript. A form with id `address-form` has the heading "Shipping address", text inputs with ids `street`, `city` and `zip`, a select with id `country` offering at least three countries, and a button labelled "Continue". Mark the street, city and zip inputs as required.
behaviours: The three text inputs carry the required attribute
The country select lists at least three options

brief: Build a unit converter titled "Unit converter". A number input with id `value`, a select with id `from-unit` and a select with id `to-unit` (kilometres, miles and metres each), and a button with id `convert-btn` labelled "Convert". Clicking it writes the converted number, rounded to two decimals, into an element with id `output`.
behaviours: 1 kilometre to miles shows 0.62
Empty input leaves #output empty or shows a message

brief: Build a live word counter with the `h1` heading "Word counter". A textarea with id `text-input` and two spans with ids `word-count` and `char-count`. Every time the user types, update `word-count` with the number of words and `char-count` with the number of characters. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Typing "hello big world" shows 3 words and 15 characters
The counts update on every keystroke

brief: Build a BMI calculator. Number inputs with ids `weight` (kilograms) and `height` (centimetres), a button with id `bmi-btn` labelled "Calculate BMI" and an element with id `bmi-result`. Clicking the button writes the BMI to one decimal and a category (Underweight, Normal, Overweight) into `bmi-result`; invalid input writes "Enter valid numbers".
behaviours: 70 kg and 175 cm gives 22.9 and Normal
Invalid input shows "Enter valid numbers"

brief: Build a password generator. A number input with id `length` (default 12), a checkbox with id `include-symbols`, a button with id `generate-btn` labelled "Generate" and a paragraph with id `password-output`. Clicking the button writes a random password of the chosen length into `password-output`; symbols are only used when the checkbox is ticked.
behaviours: The generated password has exactly the requested length
Without the checkbox only letters and digits appear

brief: Build a 25 minute focus timer. An element with id `timer-display` initially shows "25:00", a button with id `start-btn` labelled "Start" and a button with id `reset-btn` labelled "Reset". Start counts down once per second in the format mm:ss; Reset stops it and shows "25:00" again. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: After Start the display counts down each second
Reset restores 25:00

brief: Build a static sales dashboard with no JavaScript and the `h1` heading "Sales dashboard". Three `div` elements with class `card` titled "Revenue", "Users" and "Orders", each with an invented figure, and a table with id `sales` of four rows (month, units, income). It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Three cards sit side by side on desktop and stack on a phone
The table has four data rows

brief: Build a bar chart using only plain page elements. An `h1` reading "Weekly signups" and a container with id `chart`. JavaScript holds an array of seven numbers and creates one `div` with class `bar` per number inside `chart`, each with a height proportional to its value.
behaviours: Seven bars are created
The tallest bar belongs to the largest number

brief: Build a sortable people table. A table with id `people` has columns Name and Age and four invented rows. Two buttons with ids `sort-name` (labelled "Sort by name") and `sort-age` (labelled "Sort by age") re-order the rows ascending when clicked, using JavaScript.
behaviours: Clicking Sort by age orders rows from youngest to oldest
Clicking Sort by name orders them alphabetically

brief: Build a filterable task list with the `h1` heading "Task list". A text input with id `filter-input` and an unordered list with id `task-list` holding six `li` elements with class `task`. As the user types, hide every task whose text does not contain the typed text, ignoring case. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Typing "mail" hides tasks without that word
Clearing the input shows all six tasks again

brief: Build a static status page with no JavaScript. An `h1` reading "System status", and an unordered list with class `services` of four `li` elements with class `service`, each containing a service name and a `span` with class `badge` reading "Operational". It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Four services are listed
Each service has a visible Operational badge

brief: Build a number guessing game. The script picks a secret number from 1 to 100. A number input with id `guess`, a button with id `guess-btn` labelled "Guess", a paragraph with id `hint` and a span with id `attempts`. Each guess writes "Too high", "Too low" or "Correct" into `hint` and increases the count in `attempts`.
behaviours: A guess above the secret shows "Too high"
The attempts counter increases on every guess

brief: Build tic-tac-toe for two players. A container with id `board` holds nine buttons with class `cell`, a paragraph with id `turn` that starts as "X's turn", and a button with id `restart-btn` labelled "Restart". Clicking an empty cell places the current mark and switches turns; announce a winner in `turn`.
behaviours: Cells alternate X and O
Restart clears the board

brief: Build rock paper scissors against the computer. Buttons with ids `rock-btn`, `paper-btn` and `scissors-btn` labelled "Rock", "Paper" and "Scissors", a paragraph with id `result` and a paragraph with id `score` that starts as "Score: 0 - 0". Each click plays a random computer move, writes the outcome into `result` and updates `score`. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Each click shows a win, loss or draw
The score changes after a win or loss

brief: Build a memory card game with eight elements of class `card` showing four pairs of letters, hidden until clicked. Clicking two cards reveals them; matching pairs stay open, others flip back after one second. A span with id `moves` counts attempts and a button with id `reset-btn` labelled "New game" reshuffles.
behaviours: A matching pair stays face up
The moves counter goes up after every two clicks

brief: Build a ten second clicking game with the heading "Click challenge". A button with id `start-btn` labelled "Start", a button with id `click-btn` labelled "Click me!", a span with id `count` and a span with id `time-left`. After Start, count clicks until `time-left` reaches 0, then disable `click-btn`. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: The timer counts down from 10
Clicks after time is up are ignored

brief: Build a static team page with no JavaScript. An `h1` reading "Our team" and a `section` with class `team` holding four `article` elements with class `member`, each with an `h2` name and a paragraph with class `role`. Use a responsive grid that becomes one column on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Four member cards are shown
Cards stack in one column on a narrow screen

brief: Build a static FAQ page with no JavaScript using native disclosure elements. An `h1` reading "FAQ" and four `details` elements with class `faq`, each with a `summary` question and a paragraph answer. All must start collapsed.
behaviours: Four questions are listed
Clicking a question expands its answer without JavaScript

brief: Build a static recipe card with no JavaScript. An `h1` reading "Pancakes", a paragraph with class `time` containing "Ready in 20 minutes", an unordered list with id `ingredients` of at least five items and an ordered list with id `steps` of at least four steps. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Ingredients and steps are separate lists
Text is readable on a phone screen

brief: Build a static landing page with no JavaScript. A `header` with class `hero` containing an `h1` reading "Plan trips together" and a link with class `cta` labelled "Get started", then a `section` with class `features` of three `div` elements with class `feature`. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: The hero shows the headline and the call-to-action link
Three feature blocks follow

brief: Build a small portfolio page with the `h1` heading "My projects", a button with id `theme-toggle` labelled "Toggle theme" and a `section` with class `projects` of three project blurbs. Clicking the button adds or removes the class `dark` on the `body` element, and the CSS restyles the page when it is present.
behaviours: Clicking the button toggles the dark class on body
Dark mode changes the background and text colours

brief: Build a tabs widget inside a container with id `tabs`. Three buttons with class `tab` labelled "Overview", "Details" and "Reviews", and three `div` elements with class `panel`. Only the panel for the chosen tab is visible; the chosen button also gets the class `active`. Start on Overview.
behaviours: Clicking a tab shows only its panel
The clicked button has the active class

brief: Build a modal dialog demo. A button with id `open-modal` labelled "Open dialog" and a hidden `div` with id `modal` containing the text "Are you sure?" and a button with id `close-modal` labelled "Close". Open shows the modal over the page; Close hides it; pressing the Escape key also hides it.
behaviours: The modal is hidden on load
Escape closes the modal

brief: Build a text slide carousel with three elements of class `slide`, buttons with ids `prev-btn` and `next-btn` labelled "Previous" and "Next", and a span with id `indicator` that starts as "1 / 3". Only one slide is visible; the buttons move between slides and wrap around, updating `indicator`.
behaviours: Next moves to slide 2 and shows 2 / 3
Next on the last slide wraps to the first

brief: Build a star rating widget inside a container with id `rating`. Five buttons with class `star` showing a star character, and a paragraph with id `rating-value` that starts as "Rating: 0". Clicking the nth star fills stars 1 to n and writes "Rating: n" into `rating-value`. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Clicking the third star shows "Rating: 3"
Stars are large enough to tap on a phone

brief: Build a to-do list. A text input with id `todo-input`, a button with id `add-btn` labelled "Add" and an unordered list with id `todo-list`. Clicking Add appends the typed text as an `li` and clears the input; ignore empty text. Clicking an item toggles the class `done` on it. It must work on a phone screen about 360px wide.
behaviours: Adding "buy milk" appends an li with that text
Clicking an item toggles the done class
